AI.motivation: Robot programming is challenging, particularly when using natural language. There is a need for safer and more accessible programming methods that allow users to prototype and validate robot behaviors before physical deployment.
AI.method: A passthrough mixed-reality workspace where users place robot twins on real surfaces. The system supports two interaction modes: (1) waypoint teaching where users teach trajectories and save episodes, and (2) language-guided control where spoken/typed commands are converted to structured plans by a vision-language model. Both modes share a backend for metric grounding, embodiment-aware validation, preview, confirmation, and execution. The system supports heterogeneous robot embodiments including fixed-base manipulators, mobile bases, and humanoid robots.
AI.result: The system demonstrates mixed-reality validation as an effective safety layer for language-guided robot programming before physical deployment, working across different robot embodiments.
AI.conclusion: ORCESTRA provides an intuitive, safe approach to robot programming by combining no-code waypoint teaching with natural language control in a mixed-reality environment, with built-in validation capabilities that bridge the gap between simulation and physical reality.

title: SIPTraj: Map-Free End-to-End Trajectory Prediction via Physics-Guided Scene Interaction
summary: Trajectory prediction of surrounding agents is a prerequisite for safe planning and decision making in autonomous driving. Without high-definition (HD) maps, sensor-derived bird's-eye-view (BEV) features provide no explicit lane topology or drivable-area priors, making it inherently difficult to ground each agent in its surrounding scene context. Moreover, physical feasibility remains difficult to capture through data-driven learning alone, as kinematic constraints on agent motion cannot be explicitly encoded without structured supervision. Existing map-free predictors extract scene context in an agent-agnostic manner through a single fusion step and treat physical constraints only as output-level penalties, leaving both challenges unaddressed. We propose SIPTraj, a map-free trajectory prediction framework that jointly addresses scene grounding and physical feasibility. SIPTraj introduces a Hierarchical Agent-Scene Encoder (HASE) progressively grounding each agent in agent-guided scene evidence and refining inter-agent relations within the scene-grounded space. To tackle physical infeasibility in predicted trajectories, we develop a Physics-Guided Iterative Decoder (PGID). It conditions decoding on instantaneous kinematic states, propagating physical supervision into internal representations rather than output trajectories alone. Extensive experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 Sensor show that SIPTraj surpasses prior map-free predictors and strong map-based baselines without any HD map at inference. Our code will be released as open-source.

AI.tldr: SIPTraj is a map-free trajectory prediction framework that addresses scene grounding and physical feasibility through a Hierarchical Agent-Scene Encoder and Physics-Guided Iterative Decoder, outperforming both map-free and map-based baselines without requiring HD maps.
AI.motivation: Trajectory prediction in autonomous driving faces two key challenges without HD maps: (1) scene grounding is difficult as BEV features lack explicit lane topology or drivable-area priors, and (2) physical feasibility is hard to capture through data-driven learning alone since kinematic constraints cannot be explicitly encoded without structured supervision. Existing map-free predictors extract scene context in an agent-agnostic manner through a single fusion step and only treat physical constraints as output-level penalties.
AI.method: SIPTraj introduces two core components: (1) Hierarchical Agent-Scene Encoder (HASE) that progressively grounds each agent in agent-guided scene evidence and refines inter-agent relations within the scene-grounded space; (2) Physics-Guided Iterative Decoder (PGID) that conditions decoding on instantaneous kinematic states, propagating physical supervision into internal representations rather than output trajectories alone.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 Sensor datasets demonstrate that SIPTraj surpasses prior map-free predictors and strong map-based baselines without requiring any HD maps at inference time.
AI.conclusion: SIPTraj successfully addresses both scene grounding and physical feasibility challenges in map-free trajectory prediction, establishing a new state-of-the-art approach that works without high-definition maps.

title: StochSIPP: Safe Interval Path Planning in Stochastic Dynamic Environments
summary: Safe navigation under uncertain time-dependent blockage requires anticipating observations before committing to motion. We present StochSIPP, an exact contingent planner for temporal roadmaps with uncertain edge and vertex statuses revealed locally during execution. StochSIPP uses SIPP to generate certified-safe macro-actions that terminate at the next observation or the goal, and bounded AND/OR search over a cached action--observation graph to select actions for every reachable observation outcome. Optimistic and robust SIPP relaxations provide admissible lower and upper bounds for bounded AND/OR search. When every interval declared deterministically safe is truly safe, sensing is exact, and execution follows the planned timing, the resulting policy is provably collision-free. With correct independent probabilities and complete action and outcome generation, it minimizes expected arrival time within the roadmap and horizon. Experiments on controlled roadmap instances show that StochSIPP preserves the observed success of safe fixed-path baselines while reducing arrival time, and solves gated scenarios in which conservative fixed-path planners return no plan. A scalability study further reveals rapid growth as the number of simultaneously observed uncertain statuses increases.

AI.tldr: StochSIPP is an exact contingent planner for temporal roadmaps that generates certified-safe macro-actions and performs bounded AND/OR search over an action-observation graph to minimize expected arrival time under uncertain, time-dependent blockage.
AI.motivation: Safe navigation requires anticipating observations before committing to motion when dealing with uncertain time-dependent blockage, which traditional fixed-path planners cannot handle effectively.
AI.method: StochSIPP uses SIPP to generate certified-safe macro-actions terminating at observations or goal, performs bounded AND/OR search over a cached action-observation graph, and employs optimistic/robust SIPP relaxations to provide admissible bounds.
AI.result: Experiments show StochSIPP preserves success of safe fixed-path baselines while reducing arrival time, solves gated scenarios where fixed-path planners fail, and exhibits rapid growth in complexity as the number of simultaneously observed uncertain statuses increases.
AI.conclusion: When conditions hold (exact sensing, correct probabilities, proper execution), StochSIPP produces provably collision-free policies that minimize expected arrival time, though scalability becomes challenging with many simultaneous uncertain statuses.

title: DynamicWAM: Dual-Path Motion Conditioning for World-Action Models in Dynamic Manipulation
summary: Dynamic manipulation requires robots to infer target motion and respond promptly, yet existing World-Action Models (WAMs) typically condition only on the current frame and execute large backbones synchronously, limiting motion awareness and responsive control in dynamic scenes. We propose DynamicWAM, a compact WAM for dynamic object manipulation with dual-path motion conditioning. DynamicWAM introduces history-flow conditioning, encoding temporally aligned optical-flow frames alongside the current observation through a frozen pretrained video VAE to preserve spatial motion structure, while injecting kinematic descriptors of displacement, duration, velocity, and acceleration into the action expert to provide motion magnitude and timing. The two complementary paths are fused through joint world-action attention. A distilled compact backbone and real-time chunking (RTC)-based asynchronous execution further enable responsive control. On DOMINO, DynamicWAM achieves a 38.2% success rate and a 53.2 manipulation score, outperforming all evaluated baselines. Across 12 real-world tasks spanning linear, circular, and compound target motion, it achieves a 46.7% average success rate, exceeding the strongest baseline by 22.9 percentage points.

AI.tldr: DynamicWAM is a compact World-Action Model for dynamic object manipulation that uses dual-path motion conditioning (history-flow encoding via frozen video VAE and kinematic descriptors) fused through joint attention, enabling responsive control with a distilled backbone and RTC-based execution. It achieves 46.7% average success across 12 real-world tasks (22.9% above strongest baseline).
AI.motivation: Existing World-Action Models (WAMs) typically condition only on the current frame and execute large backbones synchronously, limiting motion awareness and responsive control in dynamic manipulation scenes.
AI.method: DynamicWAM introduces dual-path motion conditioning: (1) history-flow conditioning using frozen pretrained video VAE to encode temporally aligned optical-flow frames alongside current observation; (2) kinematic descriptors (displacement, duration, velocity, acceleration) injected into action expert. Paths fused via joint world-action attention. Uses distilled compact backbone and real-time chunking (RTC)-based asynchronous execution.
AI.result: On DOMINO: 38.2% success rate and 53.2 manipulation score, outperforming all baselines. Across 12 real-world tasks (linear, circular, compound motion): 46.7% average success rate, exceeding strongest baseline by 22.9 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: DynamicWAM effectively addresses limitations of existing WAMs in dynamic scenes by preserving spatial motion structure and providing motion magnitude/timing, enabling responsive control for complex target motion scenarios.

title: LooperMuscle: Fast and Stable Learning of Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking via Structured Mixture-of-Experts
summary: FastSAC-style methods significantly reduce humanoid motion training time but often suffer from notable performance degradation compared with PPO in whole-body tracking tasks. We target this speed-performance gap by introducing LooperMuscle, a composed expert policy learning framework that restores tracking quality while preserving high training efficiency. LooperMuscle combines a semantically structured mixture-of-experts actor, an expert-aware distributional critic, and contribution-routed replay with deferred curriculum scheduling. These three components form a closed training loop in which expert contributions guide data routing, routed data shape value learning, and value gradients in turn refine expert specialization. Empirically, our approach substantially outperforms vanilla FastSAC in motion tracking accuracy while requiring far less wall-clock time than PPO: where FastSAC trains in about 15 minutes but underperforms, and PPO achieves stronger results but requires about 6 hours, LooperMuscle recovers a substantial fraction of the remaining gap to PPO in roughly 45 minutes of simulation training, delivering practical efficiency for rapid policy iteration. The code will be released to benefit the research community at https://loopermuscle.github.io/.

AI.tldr: LooperMuscle is a composed expert policy learning framework that combines a semantically structured mixture-of-experts actor, expert-aware distributional critic, and contribution-routed replay with deferred curriculum scheduling to achieve high humanoid motion tracking accuracy while maintaining fast training efficiency.
AI.motivation: FastSAC-style methods significantly reduce humanoid motion training time but suffer notable performance degradation compared to PPO in whole-body tracking tasks. There exists a speed-performance tradeoff gap that needs to be addressed for practical rapid policy iteration.
AI.method: Three core components form a closed training loop: (1) a semantically structured mixture-of-experts actor, (2) an expert-aware distributional critic, and (3) contribution-routed replay with deferred curriculum scheduling. These components enable mutual guidance: expert contributions guide data routing, routed data shapes value learning, and value gradients refine expert specialization.
AI.result: LooperMuscle substantially outperforms vanilla FastSAC in motion tracking accuracy while requiring far less wall-clock time than PPO: it recovers a substantial fraction of PPO's performance gap in approximately 45 minutes of simulation training (vs. 15 minutes for FastSAC and 6 hours for PPO).
AI.conclusion: The approach delivers practical efficiency for rapid policy iteration, bridging the speed-performance gap between FastSAC and PPO methods. Code will be released at https://loopermuscle.github.io/.

title: RIT*: Riemannian Informed Trees for Cost-Adaptive Optimal Motion Planning
comment: Accepted in Robotics and Automation Letters
summary: We present Riemannian Informed Trees (RIT*), a planning framework that replaces Euclidean primitives in batch-informed search with their Riemannian counterparts. RIT* constructs a tighter, cost-consistent informed set, performs a nearest-neighbour search under an anisotropic distance metric, and evaluates edge costs efficiently via a cascading scheme. We further introduce a Collision-Adaptive Metric Refinement (CARM), which learns an obstacle-proximity cost field online from collision feedback, reducing the reliance on prior metric design in practical settings. Experiments across environments from 2-D to 14-D show that RIT* is competitive in low-dimensional and spatially constant-metric settings and produces substantially lower-cost solutions when the metric varies spatially in high-dimensional configuration spaces. Performance gains scale with anisotropy and dimension, reaching up to 13.0% improvement in median initial cost over BIT* in the 3-D anisotropic benchmark, up to 9.0% in median final cost over BIT* in 6-DOF manipulation, and 24.8-63.5% in a 14-DOF bimanual planning problem, where Euclidean-informed baselines degrade. Videos and code can be found here: https://muhayyuddin.github.io/ritstar/

AI.tldr: RIT* is a Riemannian-geometry-based informed search planner that replaces Euclidean primitives with Riemannian counterparts, achieving 24.8-63.5% improvements in high-dimensional anisotropic environments by constructing tighter informed sets, performing anisotropic nearest-neighbor search, and using a learned Collision-Adaptive Metric Refinement (CARM) that adapts to obstacle proximity from collision feedback.
AI.motivation: Traditional informed search planners (like BIT*) use Euclidean geometry primitives which are suboptimal in high-dimensional configuration spaces where the underlying metric varies spatially or is anisotropic. The reliance on fixed Euclidean metrics leads to less efficient sampling, larger informed sets, and higher-cost solutions in complex environments.
AI.method: RIT* replaces Euclidean primitives with Riemannian counterparts to construct a tighter, cost-consistent informed set. It performs nearest-neighbor search using an anisotropic distance metric and evaluates edge costs efficiently via a cascading scheme. The key innovation is Collision-Adaptive Metric Refinement (CARM), which learns an obstacle-proximity cost field online from collision feedback, dynamically adapting the metric to the environment.
AI.result: Experiments across 2-D to 14-D environments show RIT* is competitive in low-dimensional/spatially constant-metric settings and significantly outperforms BIT* in high-dimensional anisotropic spaces. Performance gains scale with anisotropy and dimension: 13.0% improvement in median initial cost over BIT* in 3-D anisotropic benchmark, 9.0% in median final cost in 6-DOF manipulation, and 24.8-63.5% in a 14-DOF bimanual planning problem where Euclidean baselines degrade.
AI.conclusion: Riemannian geometry provides a more appropriate foundation for planning in high-dimensional configuration spaces with spatially varying or anisotropic metrics. RIT* demonstrates that replacing Euclidean primitives with Riemannian ones, combined with online metric adaptation via collision feedback, yields substantial performance improvements in complex planning problems, with gains increasing with dimensionality and anisotropy.

title: GeminiPainter's sequence-formed pipeline comprised of perception, cognition, planning, and action stages
summary: We present an autonomous robotic portrait-generation system combining real-time face detection, AI-based sketch generation, and robotic drawing. The system captures video frames, extracts facial regions, converts them into minimalist single-line sketches using the Gemini Vision API, optimizes stroke order through graph-based path planning, and executes smooth trajectories on a 6-DoF collaborative manipulator. This perception-cognition-action pipeline integrates computer vision, neural artistic abstraction, motion optimization, and robot control. User ratings on a 5-point scale were high for sketch quality 4.33, perceived execution 4.53, and user experience 4.65, indicating recognizable, appealing, and engaging robotic portraits.

AI.tldr: An autonomous robotic portrait-generation system that integrates real-time face detection, AI-based sketch generation via Gemini Vision API, and robotic drawing on a 6-DoF manipulator, achieving high user ratings (4.33-4.65 on 5-point scale) for sketch quality, perceived execution, and user experience.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the integration of perception-cognition-action pipeline in robotics, combining computer vision, neural artistic abstraction, motion optimization, and robot control to enable autonomous creation of recognizable and appealing robotic portraits.
AI.method: A perception-cognition-action pipeline consisting of: 1) real-time face detection and facial region extraction from video frames; 2) minimalist single-line sketch generation using Gemini Vision API for neural artistic abstraction; 3) stroke order optimization via graph-based path planning; and 4) smooth trajectory execution on a 6-DoF collaborative manipulator.
AI.result: User ratings on a 5-point scale: sketch quality 4.33, perceived execution 4.53, user experience 4.65, indicating recognizable, appealing, and engaging robotic portraits with high satisfaction across all metrics.
AI.conclusion: The integrated system successfully demonstrates that autonomous robotic portrait generation is feasible and produces results that users perceive as high quality, well-executed, and engaging, validating the effectiveness of combining computer vision, neural artistic abstraction, and motion optimization in a perception-cognition-action framework.

title: Minute-Scale Training for Microrobot Navigation
summary: Microrobots hold significant potential for various applications, where targeted navigation is a basic requirement. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has recently emerged as a powerful paradigm for fully autonomous microrobot navigation. Yet, current DRL-based approaches pay limited attention to learning efficiency and effectiveness, requiring hours to days for model training. Consequently, this impedes both rapid practical deployment and parameter optimization. To address these challenges, we present a learning framework that enables effective microrobot navigation policies to be trained within minutes. In the proposed framework, we develop a fully vectorized simulator with more than 10,000 artificial vascular environments, parallelizing dynamics, LiDAR-inspired perception, and feasibility checks across thousands of environments to achieve roughly 190,000 transitions per second. To achieve effectiveness in the fast training, we propose a task-shaping-regularization (TSR) reward framework. The TSR framework accelerates convergence, improves final performance, reduces action variation by at least 33.7%, and increases obstacle clearance by at least 2.1% across all evaluated scenarios. Results show that the proposed learning framework reduces training time to under 10 minutes, while supporting zero-shot deployment across distinct microrobot types and navigation scenarios. Collectively, this framework can substantially shorten the design loop and accelerate the deployment of autonomous microrobots.

AI.tldr: A fast learning framework for microrobot navigation using deep reinforcement learning, which can train policies in under 10 minutes via a vectorized simulator and task-shaping-regularization reward framework, enabling zero-shot deployment across different microrobot types.
AI.motivation: Current DRL-based approaches for microrobot navigation require hours to days for training, which impedes rapid practical deployment and parameter optimization. The field needs more efficient training methods that can significantly reduce training time while maintaining effectiveness.
AI.method: The proposed framework consists of: 1) A fully vectorized simulator with over 10,000 artificial vascular environments that parallelizes dynamics, LiDAR-inspired perception, and feasibility checks across thousands of environments, achieving ~190,000 transitions per second; 2) A Task-Shaping-Regularization (TSR) reward framework that accelerates convergence, improves performance, reduces action variation, and increases obstacle clearance.
AI.result: The framework reduces training time to under 10 minutes, reduces action variation by at least 33.7%, increases obstacle clearance by at least 2.1%, and supports zero-shot deployment across distinct microrobot types and navigation scenarios.
AI.conclusion: This learning framework substantially shortens the design loop and accelerates the deployment of autonomous microrobots, making it feasible to rapidly iterate and optimize navigation policies in practical applications.

title: Bicycle Acrobatics with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Bicycle robots are fast and energy efficient, but their simple mechanical design and their underactuated and non-holonomic dynamics make highly agile maneuvers difficult to achieve. Here, we use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to enable a bicycle robot to learn and compose a diverse repertoire of dynamic acrobatic stunts. Using different RL formulations such as waypoint following, pose reaching, twist tracking, guided tracking, and motion imitation, the robot acquires autonomous single and multi-table forward and lateral jumps, steerable jumps, front flips, kip-ups, kip-downs, driving, wheelies, bunny hops, and three-point turns. To coordinate these behaviors, we introduce an orchestrator that transitions between policies using state-dependent triggers, enabling robust long-horizon acrobatic stunts. We validate the approach on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a custom bicycle robot, in simulation and hardware. The robot repeatedly traverses tables up to 1 m high, performs more than 15 consecutive autonomous jumps while following waypoints, handles previously unseen multi-table configurations, executes continuous repertoires of kipups, jumps, flips, kip-downs, over more than 20 consecutive trials, and performs more than 10 consecutive autonomous and steerable repertoires of wheelies, lateral jumps, and single-wheel jump downs. These results demonstrate that RL can endow bicycle robots with levels of agility previously associated primarily with legged platforms while preserving the speed and efficiency of wheeled locomotion, establishing a foundation for bicycle acrobatics.

AI.tldr: Using Reinforcement Learning, a bicycle robot learns and performs diverse dynamic acrobatic stunts (jumps, flips, wheelies, etc.) with an orchestrator coordinating policies, achieving agility levels previously associated with legged platforms while preserving wheeled locomotion efficiency.
AI.motivation: Bicycle robots are fast and energy-efficient but their simple mechanical design and underactuated/non-holonomic dynamics make highly agile maneuvers difficult. The authors aim to enable bicycle robots to achieve agility levels previously associated primarily with legged platforms while preserving the speed and efficiency of wheeled locomotion.
AI.method: Employing multiple RL formulations (waypoint following, pose reaching, twist tracking, guided tracking, motion imitation) and an orchestrator that transitions between policies using state-dependent triggers. Validation performed on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV) bicycle robot in both simulation and hardware.
AI.result: The robot successfully acquires a diverse repertoire of dynamic acrobatic stunts including single/multi-table jumps, steerable jumps, front flips, kip-ups, kip-downs, driving, wheelies, bunny hops, and three-point turns. It traverses tables up to 1m high, performs over 15 consecutive autonomous jumps with waypoint following, handles unseen multi-table configurations, executes continuous repertoires over 20+ trials, and performs over 10 consecutive autonomous/steerable wheelies and lateral jumps.
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement Learning can endow bicycle robots with agility levels previously associated primarily with legged platforms while preserving the speed and efficiency of wheeled locomotion, establishing a foundation for bicycle acrobatics and demonstrating RL's potential for enabling sophisticated dynamic behaviors in underactuated systems.

title: Stipple: Real-Time Incremental Gaussian Splatting with Visual-Inertial Tracking
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides efficient rendering of photo-realistic scenes, but its heavy preprocessing and training steps make it a poor fit for applications that require real-time reconstruction in robotics or XR. This capability is important since it allows immediate feedback and interaction with new environments. Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and simultaneous localization and mapping (VI-SLAM) systems, on the other hand, specifically target these real-time applications, which makes them a good choice for integration with 3DGS. We propose a new method that tracks and reconstructs simultaneously in real-time by leveraging an efficient visual-inertial tracking system based on Basalt together with a novel incremental method built on top of Brush, an efficient Rust-based GPU-vendor-agnostic implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting. We show that many of the heavy preprocessing and training steps of 3DGS can be replaced with a more efficient incremental training strategy that has direct access to the information generated by the visual-inertial tracking system. Furthermore, we propose and combine multiple practical improvements to increase the efficiency of the training pipeline and adapt it to run in real-time, parallel to the tracking thread. This work highlights the value of exploiting the complementary nature of SLAM and 3DGS, and how that can lead to promising results for real-time 3D reconstruction.

AI.tldr: A real-time 3D reconstruction method combining 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with visual-inertial SLAM, enabling simultaneous tracking and reconstruction by replacing heavy 3DGS preprocessing with an efficient incremental training strategy.
AI.motivation: 3DGS provides photo-realistic rendering but requires heavy preprocessing and training, making it unsuitable for real-time applications like robotics and XR where immediate feedback and interaction are critical. VIO and VI-SLAM systems target real-time applications and could complement 3DGS.
AI.method: Leverages Basalt's efficient visual-inertial tracking system and builds a novel incremental method on Brush (Rust-based GPU-vendor-agnostic 3DGS). Replaces heavy preprocessing/training with efficient incremental training with direct access to tracking system information, plus multiple practical improvements for real-time parallel training.
AI.result: Achieves real-time tracking and reconstruction, demonstrates that many heavy 3DGS preprocessing steps can be replaced with incremental training, and shows that combining SLAM and 3DGS yields promising real-time 3D reconstruction results.
AI.conclusion: Highlights the complementary nature of SLAM and 3DGS, demonstrating that their integration enables efficient real-time 3D reconstruction for applications requiring immediate feedback and interaction.

title: VertiAKD: Adaptive Off-Road Kinodynamics on Vertically Challenging Terrain
summary: Off-road mobility requires autonomous mobile robots to generalize across heterogeneous vehicle fleets and continuously changing terrain conditions. Existing cross-vehicle adaptation approaches generally assume flat terrain, while terrain-aware kinodynamic models often require platform-specific data collection and retraining. To this end, we propose VertiAKD, a unified framework for transferring and adapting off-road kinodynamic knowledge across diverse vehicles on geometrically and semantically complex terrain simultaneously. VertiAKD learns a shared mobility representation that jointly encodes vehicle configurations, trajectory transitions, and local elevation and semantic terrain features. Given limited data from a novel vehicle operating on unseen terrain, VertiAKD identifies the most relevant mobility descriptors and transfers their knowledge to initialize a terrain-aware kinodynamic model via function encoders, which is then periodically refined online from streaming observations without gradient-based retraining. We evaluate VertiAKD in the Verti-Bench simulator, built on the Chrono multi-physics engine, and on five physical configurations of the Verti-4-Wheeler platform. With only one minute of new trajectory data and associated terrain features, VertiAKD reduces long-horizon prediction error by up to 34.52% over direct mobility descriptor transfer across diverse unseen vehicle configurations and 94.43% over competing baselines. We further demonstrate robust closed-loop trajectory tracking in both simulation and physical experiments, highlighting the effectiveness of terrain-aware cross-vehicle knowledge transfer for accurate modeling and reliable off-road navigation.

AI.tldr: VertiAKD is a unified framework for cross-vehicle off-road kinodynamic knowledge transfer that learns shared mobility representations and adapts models with minimal data, achieving up to 94.43% reduction in prediction error over baselines.
AI.motivation: Off-road mobile robots need to generalize across heterogeneous vehicle fleets and continuously changing terrain conditions. Existing approaches are limited: cross-vehicle adaptation methods generally assume flat terrain, while terrain-aware kinodynamic models require platform-specific data collection and retraining, making them impractical for rapid adaptation to new vehicles or terrains.
AI.method: VertiAKD learns a shared mobility representation that jointly encodes vehicle configurations, trajectory transitions, and local elevation and semantic terrain features. Given limited data from a novel vehicle on unseen terrain, it identifies relevant mobility descriptors and transfers knowledge to initialize a terrain-aware kinodynamic model via function encoders. The model is then refined periodically from streaming observations without gradient-based retraining.
AI.result: Evaluated on Verti-Bench simulator (based on Chrono multi-physics engine) and five physical configurations of the Verti-4-Wheeler platform. With only one minute of new trajectory data, VertiAKD reduces long-horizon prediction error by 34.52% over direct mobility descriptor transfer and 94.43% over competing baselines. Demonstrates robust closed-loop trajectory tracking in both simulation and physical experiments.
AI.conclusion: VertiAKD demonstrates effective terrain-aware cross-vehicle knowledge transfer for accurate modeling and reliable off-road navigation. The framework enables rapid adaptation to new vehicles with minimal data, addressing a critical gap in off-road mobile robotics where platform-specific data collection is impractical.

title: GraRe: Grasp Candidate Re-Ranking for Frozen 6-DoF Grasp Detectors
comment: 24 pages, 32 figures. Supplementary material is included
summary: Existing 6-DoF grasp detectors typically rank grasp candidates by detector confidence. However, our analysis on GraspNet-1Billion shows that detector confidence is often poorly aligned with grasp quality, causing successful grasp candidates to be ranked too low during execution. Motivated by this observation, we formulate grasp candidate re-ranking as a separate task for frozen detectors, aiming to improve candidate ordering without changing the detector or its grasp candidates. We propose GraRe, which estimates grasp quality from candidate attributes, shell-stratified local geometry, and object context. Candidate attributes condition the local geometric and object-context representations, and a Transformer fuses all three feature types. The predicted quality is combined with detector confidence to produce the final ranking. Experiments on GraspNet-1Billion with three frozen detectors show consistent improvements, with gains of up to 13.60 points in Average AP. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate robust grasping in cluttered scenes. These results show that improving candidate ranking provides a practical way to enhance frozen 6-DoF grasp detectors.

AI.tldr: GraRe is a grasp candidate re-ranking method that improves frozen 6-DoF grasp detectors by estimating grasp quality from candidate attributes, shell-stratified local geometry, and object context, achieving up to 13.60 points Average AP improvement.
AI.motivation: Existing 6-DoF grasp detectors rank candidates by detector confidence, but this is poorly aligned with actual grasp quality, causing successful candidates to be ranked too low during execution.
AI.method: GraRe estimates grasp quality by conditioning local geometric and object-context representations on candidate attributes, using a Transformer to fuse all three feature types (candidate attributes, shell-stratified local geometry, and object context). The predicted quality is combined with detector confidence for final ranking.
AI.result: Experiments on GraspNet-1Billion with three frozen detectors show consistent improvements, with gains of up to 13.60 points in Average AP. Real-robot experiments demonstrate robust grasping in cluttered scenes.
AI.conclusion: Improving candidate ranking provides a practical way to enhance frozen 6-DoF grasp detectors without changing the detector or its grasp candidates.

title: FreqNav: Stage-Wise Frequency Routing for Object-Oriented Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Object-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires searching for a described target and landing on it precisely, under long-horizon and closed-loop control. Guided by a target-descriptive instruction during navigation, perceptual priorities dynamically evolve: early-stage exploration prioritizes low-frequency spatial layout, and then shifts to high-frequency target details. Existing VLN methods model the varying perceptual requirements across navigation stages with identical visual tokens, leading to interference from irrelevant objects and background clutter. To this end, we therefore formulate long-horizon aerial navigation as a frequencypreference shift from spatial structure to local detail and propose FreqNav, a lightweight frequency-routing adaptive perception framework. Under a fixed computational budget, FreqNav dynamically reallocates visual tokens across frequency components according to the current navigation stage. A Frequency Token Router selects stage-relevant visual representations from dual-view observations, while a Phase-dependent Grounding Module anchors visual evidence through explicit supervision. A Diffusion Transformer then predicts smooth trajectories for continuous control. Experiments show that FreqNav outperforms strong baselines while achieving approximately 3x faster inference. Real-world deployment further demonstrates its effectiveness, efficiency, and practical potential for long-horizon aerial autonomy.

AI.tldr: FreqNav is a lightweight frequency-routing adaptive perception framework for object-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN) that dynamically reallocates visual tokens across frequency components based on navigation stage, achieving 3x faster inference while outperforming strong baselines.
AI.motivation: Aerial VLN requires precise target landing under long-horizon closed-loop control. Existing methods model varying perceptual requirements with identical visual tokens, causing interference from irrelevant objects and background clutter. Perceptual priorities actually evolve: early stages prioritize low-frequency spatial layout, then shift to high-frequency target details.
AI.method: FreqNav (Frequency-routing Adaptive Perception Framework) with three key components: (1) Frequency Token Router selects stage-relevant visual representations from dual-view observations; (2) Phase-dependent Grounding Module anchors visual evidence through explicit supervision; (3) Diffusion Transformer predicts smooth trajectories for continuous control.
AI.result: FreqNav outperforms strong baselines while achieving approximately 3x faster inference. Real-world deployment demonstrates its effectiveness, efficiency, and practical potential for long-horizon aerial autonomy.
AI.conclusion: The frequency-routing approach effectively addresses the dynamic perceptual requirements of aerial VLN by reallocating computational resources based on navigation stage, making it both more accurate and significantly more efficient than existing methods.

title: RL Bootstrapping of OpenVLA-OFT for a Novel Robot Embodiment
summary: Adapting a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a new robot usually assumes embodiment-specific demonstrations. This assumption is especially restrictive for custom robots whose morphology differs strongly from the manipulators seen in large robot datasets. We study a harder setting: zero-demo embodiment alignment of OpenVLA-OFT on a cable-driven parallel robot (CDPR) with a simple gripper and a previously unseen control interface. Instead of supervised fine-tuning, we use reinforcement learning in simulation with dense geometric rewards computed from simulator state. The training is performed in two stages: a PPO stage for directional motion primitives, followed by GRPO continuation from the PPO checkpoint with an expanded instruction space that includes object-conditioned commands. On the four shared directional instructions, the average held-out success rate improves from 34.25\% after PPO to 53.50\% after PPO$\rightarrow$GRPO, with especially large gains on \texttt{move left} and \texttt{move backward}. In the GRPO stage we additionally introduce \texttt{move to <object>} over eight target objects and obtain 39/400 = 9.75\% strict success, while qualitative rollouts frequently show correct target-directed approach behavior before late-stage instability. Compared with prior OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT results, which rely on demonstration datasets and mostly standard rigid-arm embodiments, our method uses no embodiment-specific dataset at all. The results do not yet establish robust manipulation, but they provide stronger evidence that RL-only bootstrapping can create the first usable language-conditioned controller for a genuinely novel embodiment.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates RL-only bootstrapping to adapt a pretrained VLA policy (OpenVLA-OFT) to a novel cable-driven parallel robot (CDPR) without any embodiment-specific demonstrations, achieving significant success rate improvements from 34.25% to 53.50% through two-stage training (PPO → GRPO).
AI.motivation: Adapting pretrained vision-language-action policies to new robots typically requires embodiment-specific demonstrations, which is restrictive for custom robots with morphologies different from those in large robot datasets. This study explores a challenging zero-demo setting where the robot's embodiment (cable-driven parallel robot) and control interface are both previously unseen.
AI.method: Two-stage reinforcement learning approach in simulation with dense geometric rewards: (1) PPO training for directional motion primitives, (2) GRPO continuation with expanded instruction space including object-conditioned commands. The method requires no embodiment-specific demonstration data.
AI.result: On four shared directional instructions, average held-out success rate improved from 34.25% after PPO to 53.50% after PPO→GRPO, with especially large gains on "move left" and "move backward" commands. With object-conditioned commands on eight target objects, achieved 39/400 = 9.75% strict success rate. Qualitative rollouts show correct target-directed approach behavior despite late-stage instability.
AI.conclusion: While not yet establishing robust manipulation, the results provide strong evidence that RL-only bootstrapping can create the first usable language-conditioned controller for a genuinely novel embodiment without any embodiment-specific dataset, demonstrating that language-conditioned control is possible through purely simulation-based RL training.

title: KING: Embodiment-Aware Kinematic Graph Neural Network for Unified Motion Representation of Legged and Wheeled Robots
summary: Kinematic models provide reliable motion constraints for odometry estimation in featureless environments, where exteroceptive sensing degrades and IMU integration drifts. Learning-based kinematic models can achieve more accurate odometry estimation than model-based methods by capturing nonlinear effects; however, most existing learning-based models are trained on a single embodiment and generalize poorly to new embodiments. This generalization is difficult because the meanings and structures of proprioceptive measurements vary across embodiments, including the number of joints and ground-contact elements (e.g., wheels, feet). To address this challenge, we propose KING, a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based kinematic model that explicitly incorporates robot embodiments by representing them as a common graph. We show that wheel and leg kinematic models can be expressed by a unified representation, enabling a single model for both wheeled and legged robots. Trained on datasets spanning diverse embodiments, KING provides a unified representation of wheeled and legged kinematics and achieves high-accuracy odometry estimation in real environments. KING estimates accurate odometry using only an embodiment description (e.g., a URDF file) and on-board proprioception (encoders and an IMU) and can be adapted to new robot embodiments through few-shot learning with only one minute of data, avoiding retraining from scratch on a new dataset for each robot. The project page is available at: https://smrg-aist.github.io/king_project_page/

AI.tldr: KING is a Graph Neural Network-based kinematic model that enables unified odometry estimation for both wheeled and legged robots across different embodiments, with few-shot adaptation capabilities.
AI.motivation: Learning-based kinematic models capture nonlinear effects better than model-based methods but suffer from poor generalization across different robot embodiments due to varying proprioceptive measurement structures (joint counts, ground-contact elements). Existing approaches require training on single embodiments, making adaptation to new robots inefficient.
AI.method: KING represents robot embodiments as a common graph structure, enabling a unified representation for wheel and leg kinematic models. It uses embodiment descriptions (e.g., URDF files) combined with on-board proprioception (encoders and IMU) to estimate odometry. The GNN architecture captures relationships across different robotic forms.
AI.result: KING achieves high-accuracy odometry estimation in real environments. It provides a unified representation of wheeled and legged kinematics and can adapt to new robot embodiments through few-shot learning with only one minute of data, avoiding retraining from scratch.
AI.conclusion: KING successfully bridges the gap between learning-based and model-based kinematic models by explicitly incorporating robot embodiments through graph representation, enabling efficient cross-embodiment generalization for odometry estimation in diverse robotic platforms.

title: Sampling-Based Visibility Task Planning
summary: Robot Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) algorithms enable autonomous operation by incorporating the specific functions and constraints of end-effector tools, such as grippers or soldering irons, directly into the planning process. In this paper, we explore sampling-based TAMP algorithms specifically designed for a critical subset of devices whose unique properties make traditional planning methods ineffective. Visibility-based instruments, such as exteroceptive sensors, cameras, flashlights and directional antennas, are essential across a vast array of human activities. The unique properties of these devices, and particularly, their field-of-view, render many widely used heuristics and distance metrics less effective. We introduce two new sampling-based algorithms, VisPRM and VisRRT, designed to tackle visibility-based tasks. VisPRM employs a hierarchical decomposition of the environment, leveraging the concept of visibility integrity, to efficiently sample configurations with a clear line-of-sight to the target. A specialized Inverse Kinematics solver enables VisRRT to "glance" in the direction of the target at opportune moments, facilitating the rapid discovery of key configurations. We show that VisPRM and VisRRT achieve a higher success rate and faster runtimes compared to adaptations of RRT, PRM and VIR, through both simulated and physical experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces VisPRM and VisRRT, two sampling-based TAMP algorithms specifically designed for visibility-based instruments (e.g., cameras, flashlights) that have unique field-of-view constraints, achieving higher success rates and faster runtimes compared to traditional RRT, PRM, and VIR adaptations.
AI.motivation: Traditional TAMP algorithms struggle with visibility-based instruments (exteroceptive sensors, cameras, flashlights, directional antennas) due to their unique field-of-view properties, rendering many widely used heuristics and distance metrics ineffective for planning tasks involving these devices.
AI.method: Two novel sampling-based algorithms are introduced: VisPRM (Visibility-based Probabilistic Roadmap) uses hierarchical environment decomposition and the concept of visibility integrity to efficiently sample configurations with clear line-of-sight to targets; VisRRT (Visibility-based Rapidly-exploring Random Tree) employs a specialized Inverse Kinematics solver to "glance" in the direction of targets at opportune moments, facilitating rapid discovery of key configurations.
AI.result: Both VisPRM and VisRRT achieve higher success rates and faster runtimes compared to adaptations of RRT, PRM, and VIR across both simulated and physical experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VisPRM and VisRRT algorithms successfully address the unique challenges posed by visibility-based instruments in TAMP tasks, demonstrating superior performance over traditional planning methods through their specialized approaches to handling field-of-view constraints and visibility integrity.

title: VLAGuard: A Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Physical Attention Hijacking in Vision-Language-Action Robots within Wireless Sensor Networks
comment: 32 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in Ad Hoc & Sensor Wireless Networks (AHSWN)
summary: Deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robots as mobile edge nodes within wireless sensor networks (WSNs) requires robust protection against physical adversarial threats. We present VLAGuard, a framework to assess and mitigate a critical vulnerability: policy-critical action-to-vision attention hijacking. We first introduce a stress-test module, Visuomotor Attention-guided Semantic Attack (VASA), using printable patches to severely distract the robot's action-conditioned cross-attention. To counter this, we propose Attention-Protective Fine-Tuning (APFT), a defense that stabilizes spatiotemporal attention and enforces geometric consistency with zero inference overhead. Evaluations across simulated and physical WSN-assisted smart environments demonstrate significant robustness gains. APFT reduces the OpenVLA failure rate from 100.0% to 25.9% in LIBERO simulations. Furthermore, across 2,000 real-world trials, APFT improves the average success rate from 23.0% to 67.4% under severe patch attacks. This highlights that protecting attention pathways is important for improving the robustness of VLA-driven edge nodes in sensor networks.

AI.tldr: VLAGuard is a framework that assesses and mitigates policy-critical action-to-vision attention hijacking in Vision-Language-Action robots deployed as mobile edge nodes in wireless sensor networks. It introduces VASA stress-test and APFT defense mechanism.
AI.motivation: Deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robots as mobile edge nodes in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) requires protection against physical adversarial threats, specifically attention hijacking where visual attention can be manipulated to cause policy-critical failures.
AI.method: The framework comprises two key components: (1) VASA (Visuomotor Attention-guided Semantic Attack) - a stress-test module using printable patches to distract the robot's action-conditioned cross-attention; (2) APFT (Attention-Protective Fine-Tuning) - a defense that stabilizes spatiotemporal attention and enforces geometric consistency with zero inference overhead.
AI.result: Significant robustness gains demonstrated across evaluations: In LIBERO simulations, OpenVLA failure rate reduced from 100.0% to 25.9%; across 2,000 real-world trials, average success rate improved from 23.0% to 67.4% under severe patch attacks.
AI.conclusion: Protecting attention pathways is critical for improving the robustness of VLA-driven edge nodes in sensor networks, as demonstrated by the substantial improvement in task success rates and reduction in failure rates when attention protection mechanisms are applied.

title: Diffusion-Based Body Schema Learning Enabling Abnormal-State Adaptation in Musculoskeletal Robots
comment: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), website - https://haraduka.github.io/muscle-diffusion/
summary: Musculoskeletal robots require an internal body schema that remains consistent under a wide range of physical state changes, including abnormalities such as muscle rupture and actuator jamming. Conventional approaches based on autoencoders or variational autoencoders learn average behaviors by projecting sensor and actuator signals into a low-dimensional latent space; however, exploration within the latent space alone has limited capability to handle out-of-distribution or abnormal states that are not included in the training data. To address this limitation, this study proposes a diffusion-based framework for body schema learning in musculoskeletal robots. Unlike generative models that operate through low-dimensional latent spaces, diffusion models can directly and iteratively estimate physically consistent sensor and actuator values in the high-dimensional space through a denoising process, even under partial observations and constraints, without requiring retraining. By formulating body schema adaptation as a gradient-guided denoising process, the proposed method enables adaptive estimation of appropriate muscle lengths and muscle tensions even under abnormal conditions such as muscle rupture and actuator jamming. The validity of the proposed framework is verified through simulation experiments using a musculoskeletal robot model.

AI.tldr: A diffusion-based framework for body schema learning in musculoskeletal robots that enables physically consistent estimation of sensor and actuator values under abnormal conditions like muscle rupture and actuator jamming, without requiring retraining.
AI.motivation: Musculoskeletal robots require an internal body schema that remains consistent despite physical state changes such as muscle rupture and actuator jamming. Conventional approaches using autoencoders or variational autoencoders learn average behaviors through low-dimensional latent spaces, which have limited capability to handle out-of-distribution or abnormal states not present in training data.
AI.method: A diffusion-based framework is proposed that directly and iteratively estimates physically consistent sensor and actuator values in high-dimensional space through a denoising process. The body schema adaptation is formulated as a gradient-guided denoising process that works under partial observations and constraints without requiring retraining.
AI.result: The proposed method enables adaptive estimation of appropriate muscle lengths and muscle tensions even under abnormal conditions such as muscle rupture and actuator jamming.
AI.conclusion: The validity of the proposed framework is verified through simulation experiments using a musculoskeletal robot model.

title: WAM-Diff2: Hierarchical AR-to-Diffusion Distillation for Highly Efficient Autonomous Driving VLA
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving; however, their efficient deployment is severely constrained by high computational latency and exposure bias arising from sequential autoregressive decoding. Conversely, while specialized diffusion policies enable low-latency, parallel execution, training them from scratch typically yields narrow, single-task architectures that lack holistic visual-linguistic reasoning. Successfully transforming pre-trained autoregressive generalists into parallel diffusion models could combine multi-task cognitive intelligence with execution efficiency, yet this transition presents a formidable architectural challenge due to mismatched attention patterns (causal versus bidirectional) and divergent optimization objectives. To bridge this divide, we introduce WAM-Diff2, a multi-task discrete diffusion VLA framework powered by a three-stage hierarchical distillation strategy. By structuring the architectural shift through progressive block-wise adaptation, block-wise distillation, and model-wise cross-scale distillation, WAM-Diff2 preserves the underlying semantic foundations of the base model while accelerating inference. Extensive evaluations across driving understanding, perception, and planning benchmarks demonstrate that WAM-Diff2 effectively mitigates exposure bias and achieves performance parity with autoregressive baselines. Crucially, the autoregressive-to-diffusion transition yields a 2.8x decoding speedup, which scales to an ultimate 15.1x acceleration when combined with system-level optimizations including FlashInfer and CUDA Graphs.

AI.tldr: WAM-Diff2 transforms autoregressive Vision-Language-Action models into efficient parallel diffusion models for autonomous driving through a three-stage hierarchical distillation strategy, achieving 2.8-15.1x speedup while maintaining performance parity.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive VLA models suffer from high latency and exposure bias due to sequential decoding, while specialized diffusion policies lack multi-task cognitive intelligence. The goal is to combine multi-task visual-linguistic reasoning with low-latency parallel execution.
AI.method: A three-stage hierarchical distillation strategy: (1) progressive block-wise adaptation for architectural shift, (2) block-wise distillation for local knowledge transfer, (3) model-wise cross-scale distillation for global semantic preservation.
AI.result: WAM-Diff2 achieves performance parity with autoregressive baselines while delivering 2.8x decoding speedup, scaling to 15.1x acceleration with FlashInfer and CUDA Graphs optimizations.
AI.conclusion: Successfully bridges the autoregressive-to-diffusion transition, enabling efficient deployment of multi-task VLA models for autonomous driving by preserving semantic foundations while accelerating inference through parallel execution.

title: OC-VLA++: Monocular Geometry-Guided Cross-View Consistency for Viewpoint-Robust Robotic Manipulation
summary: We propose OC-VLA++, an extension of OC-VLA for viewpoint generalization under limited camera coverage. While OC-VLA grounds robot actions in the camera coordinate system to align action supervision with visual observations, camera-space grounding alone can still overfit to the few viewpoints observed during training. OC-VLA++ addresses this limitation by introducing geometry-guided paired-view supervision and an explicit cross-view action-equivariance objective. Given paired observations of the same manipulation scene from geometrically related viewpoints, the model is trained such that their camera-space predictions correspond to the same robot-frame action. This objective explicitly supervises how action predictions should transform across viewpoints, rather than relying solely on image-level augmentation. Experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in unseen-view generalization under limited camera coverage, with performance degrading more gracefully under increasing camera displacement. These results establish cross-view action equivariance as an effective complement to observation-centric action grounding for robust real-world deployment.

AI.tldr: OC-VLA++ extends OC-VLA for viewpoint generalization under limited camera coverage by introducing geometry-guided paired-view supervision and an explicit cross-view action-equivariance objective.
AI.motivation: Camera-space grounding alone can overfit to few training viewpoints; need better generalization under limited camera coverage.
AI.method: Introduces geometry-guided paired-view supervision and explicit cross-view action-equivariance objective. The model is trained such that camera-space predictions from geometrically related viewpoints correspond to the same robot-frame action.
AI.result: Substantial improvements in unseen-view generalization under limited camera coverage; performance degrades more gracefully under increasing camera displacement.
AI.conclusion: Cross-view action equivariance is established as an effective complement to observation-centric action grounding for robust real-world deployment.

title: VespaSeg: A Resource-Aware Ground-then-Segment Pipeline for Referring Expression Segmentation
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Code and result artifacts: https://github.com/Savidilsh/VespaSeg
summary: Referring expression segmentation requires language conditioned localization and pixel-accurate masks, but monolithic models can be costly to deploy. We present VespaSeg, a modular pipeline that grounds a text query with a compact vision-language model and converts the predicted box to a mask with MobileSAM. We study Florence-2-base, Florence-2-large, and Moondream2 grounders together with targeted adaptation of the grounding and segmentation stages. Under a repository-specific RefCOCO validation protocol containing the first expression for each of 3,811 referenced-object records, the adapted Florence-2-base pipeline obtains 73.64 mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 84.60 precision at IoU 0.5. On an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada GPU it processes 22.8 cached-image queries per second with 2.20 GB mean allocated GPU memory. A matched 500-query comparison gives 73.73 mIoU for Florence-2-base and 72.82 for Florence-2-large, while the base model is 1.70 times faster and uses 1.17 GB less allocated memory. Ablations show that ground-truth-box adaptation raises MobileSAM mIoU from 82.22 to 86.61 and that reducing the Florence-2 output-token budget from 64 to 32 preserves accuracy. These results support compact, modular grounding and segmentation, while also exposing the need for evaluation on the complete standard RefCOCO expression splits and deployment hardware.

AI.tldr: VespaSeg introduces a modular pipeline for referring expression segmentation that combines a compact vision-language model (Florence-2-base) with MobileSAM for efficient mask generation, achieving 73.64 mIoU with 22.8 queries/second on an RTX 6000 Ada GPU.
AI.motivation: Monolithic models for referring expression segmentation are costly to deploy; the authors seek a modular approach that balances accuracy with computational efficiency.
AI.method: A two-stage modular pipeline: (1) ground text query using a compact vision-language model (Florence-2-base/large or Moondream2), (2) convert predicted box to mask using MobileSAM with ground-truth-box adaptation. The study evaluates Florence-2-base, Florence-2-large, and Moondream2 with targeted adaptation of grounding and segmentation stages.
AI.result: The adapted Florence-2-base pipeline achieves 73.64 mIoU and 84.60 precision at IoU 0.5, processes 22.8 cached-image queries per second with 2.20 GB GPU memory, and outperforms Florence-2-large in both speed (1.70× faster) and memory efficiency (1.17 GB less). Ground-truth-box adaptation raises MobileSAM mIoU from 82.22 to 86.61.
AI.conclusion: Compact, modular grounding and segmentation are viable alternatives to monolithic models. However, evaluation should be expanded to the complete standard RefCOCO expression splits and deployment hardware to better assess real-world performance.

title: Sparse Meets Dense: Correspondence Guided Robotic Manipulation with Rigid-Deformable Interactions
summary: Manipulation involving rigid-deformable interactions, such as hanging clothes or dressing humans, is common in daily life, making it essential for household robots. Compared to single-object manipulation or interactions between rigid bodies, these tasks are particularly challenging due to the rich multi-point contacts and the complex dynamics of the deformable bodies during interaction. Therefore, object-centric representations such as 6D poses or structural points without task-specific information become insufficient for these interactions. In this work, we propose a hybrid correspondence-based representation tailored for rigid-deformable interactions. First, to capture intricate interaction information, we introduce structure-, task-, and interaction-aware sparse keypoints. The keypoints are generated based on the global structures of both rigid and deformable objects, and filtered by their local interaction contacts. However, tracking these sparse keypoints through the interaction remains difficult due to the high-dimensional dynamics of deformable objects. Therefore, we further construct dense correspondences on the deformable objects for accurate keypoint tracking throughout the manipulation. This hybrid design combines the advantages of both representations: sparse keypoints encode rich, task-specific information for fine-grained manipulation, while dense correspondences ensure efficient tracking and generalization to novel deformations, shapes, and scenarios. Together, they enable one-shot transfer to new tasks with minimal demonstrations. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and broad applicability of our method.

AI.tldr: A hybrid correspondence-based representation combining sparse task-aware keypoints with dense correspondences for effective rigid-deformable manipulation tasks, enabling one-shot transfer with minimal demonstrations.
AI.motivation: Manipulation involving rigid-deformable interactions (e.g., hanging clothes, dressing) is common in daily life but challenging due to rich multi-point contacts and complex deformable body dynamics. Existing object-centric representations (6D poses, structural points) lack task-specific information and are insufficient for these interactions.
AI.method: 1. Introduces structure-, task-, and interaction-aware sparse keypoints generated from global structures and filtered by local interaction contacts; 2. Constructs dense correspondences on deformable objects for accurate keypoint tracking; 3. Hybrid design combining sparse keypoints (rich task-specific information) and dense correspondences (efficient tracking and generalization).
AI.result: The method enables one-shot transfer to new tasks with minimal demonstrations. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness and broad applicability across different deformations, shapes, and scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid correspondence-based representation effectively addresses the challenges of rigid-deformable manipulation by combining sparse task-specific information with dense tracking capabilities, providing a robust framework for household robots to perform complex manipulative tasks.

title: CAAT: Contact-Aware Attention Scaling and Tactile Masking for Data-Efficient Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: In contact-rich manipulation, visual observations primarily guide motion in free space, whereas tactile observations become particularly informative during contact. However, standard Transformer-based visuo-tactile policies typically rely on either token concatenation or learnable gating. These approaches lack explicit contact-aware priors, making it difficult to efficiently learn effective cross-modal representations from demonstrations. To address this limitation, we propose CAAT, a lightweight contact-aware framework that explicitly incorporates contact priors through attention scaling and dynamic tactile masking. Specifically, CAAT emphasizes visual information before contact and tactile information during contact. It also suppresses static background tokens by comparing the current tactile observation with a non-contact reference. CAAT can be integrated into commonly used Transformer-based policies without modifying their action decoders. In simulation, integrating CAAT with ACT improves the average success rate by 18.0 percentage points over direct visuo-tactile fusion and by 10.0 percentage points over gated fusion. In real-world experiments using a visuo-tactile UMI platform, CAAT achieves an average success rate of 60.0% across ACT, Diffusion Policy, and $π_0$, outperforming the strongest baseline by an average of 21.1 percentage points. These results demonstrate that explicit contact priors and dynamic tactile masking are effective in improving visuo-tactile policy learning and task performance of diverse policy architectures. https://mrjiangjm.github.io/caat/

AI.tldr: CAAT is a contact-aware Transformer framework that improves visuo-tactile manipulation policies by incorporating explicit contact priors through attention scaling and dynamic tactile masking.
AI.motivation: Standard Transformer-based visuo-tactile policies use token concatenation or learnable gating, but these lack explicit contact-aware priors, making it difficult to efficiently learn effective cross-modal representations from demonstrations.
AI.method: CAAT explicitly incorporates contact priors through: (1) attention scaling to emphasize visual information before contact and tactile information during contact, (2) dynamic tactile masking, and (3) suppression of static background tokens by comparing current tactile observation with non-contact reference. The framework integrates into Transformer-based policies without modifying action decoders.
AI.result: In simulation with ACT: +18.0 pp over direct visuo-tactile fusion and +10.0 pp over gated fusion. In real-world UMI experiments across ACT, Diffusion Policy, and π0: 60.0% success rate, outperforming strongest baseline by 21.1 pp.
AI.conclusion: Explicit contact priors and dynamic tactile masking effectively improve visuo-tactile policy learning and task performance across diverse policy architectures, demonstrating the value of incorporating contact-aware mechanisms into visuo-tactile perception systems.

title: FeDepth: Federated Learning for Depth Estimation under Robot Heterogeneity
comment: Accepted at ECCV 2026. Ganghyeon Lee and Inha Lee contributed equally. Kyungdon Joo is the corresponding author
summary: Although recent robot perception research emphasizes training on data from diverse environments to improve generalization, most existing methods still rely on centralized learning, which is inefficient and difficult to scale across heterogeneous robot platforms. Federated learning (FL) offers an alternative by enabling distributed training without raw data transfer, but it suffers from severe performance degradation under domain shifts caused by heterogeneity across clients. In real robotic deployments, data distributions often overlap across platforms, environments, and sensing conditions, making it difficult to partition clients into clearly separated domains. However, this characteristic breaks the assumption of clearly separable client domains commonly used in clustered FL. To address this gap in robot perception, particularly in depth estimation, we introduce two realistic and unexplored non-IID scenarios that reflect heterogeneity in terms of platform, environment, and depth distribution. We then propose FeDepth, a descriptor-based clustered FL framework that models client relationships through soft clustering. Unlike hard clustering methods that assume clearly separated clusters, FeDepth allows clients to participate in multiple clusters, capturing continuous and ambiguous domain transitions commonly observed in robotic environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FeDepth consistently improves robustness over standard FL and clustered FL baselines across multiple depth estimation architectures, providing a practical and effective solution for federated robot perception. Our project page is available at https://vision3d-lab.github.io/fedepth/.

AI.tldr: FeDepth is a descriptor-based clustered FL framework for federated robot perception that uses soft clustering to handle ambiguous domain transitions in depth estimation tasks, outperforming standard and clustered FL baselines across multiple architectures.
AI.motivation: Centralized learning is inefficient for scaling across heterogeneous robot platforms, while standard FL suffers performance degradation under domain shifts. Real robotic deployments have overlapping data distributions across platforms, environments, and sensing conditions, breaking the assumption of clearly separable client domains used in clustered FL.
AI.method: FeDepth introduces realistic non-IID scenarios reflecting heterogeneity in platform, environment, and depth distribution. It uses a descriptor-based clustered FL framework with soft clustering (rather than hard clustering) that allows clients to participate in multiple clusters, capturing continuous and ambiguous domain transitions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate FeDepth consistently improves robustness over standard FL and clustered FL baselines across multiple depth estimation architectures.
AI.conclusion: FeDepth provides a practical and effective solution for federated robot perception, addressing the challenge of ambiguous domain transitions in real-world robotic deployments.

title: Complete Motion Planning using Workspace-Fibered Decomposition for nR-Planar Manipulator
summary: We propose a workspace-fibered decomposition framework for motion planning in nR planar redundant manipulators operating in cluttered environments. Rather than planning directly in the full n-dimensional configuration space, the method incrementally constructs obstacle-constrained reachable workspaces of lower-dimensional non-redundant sub-chains and recursively lifts them through redundant orientation fibers. This yields a sequence of reduced planning manifolds that preserve branch-consistent reachability structure while avoiding explicit construction of the full configuration-space obstacle geometry. We first establish that, for planar position-only manipulators, the obstacle-constrained reachable workspace induced by the minimal non-redundant sub-chain provides an exact characterization of feasibility with respect to the connected component of the start configuration, enabling early infeasibility detection prior to introducing redundant degrees of freedom (DOF). We then introduce an incremental fiber-lifting procedure that propagates reachable workspace structure through successive redundant links while enforcing local inverse-kinematic branch consistency using Jacobian determinant continuity constraints. The resulting representation admits efficient reduced-space planning directly on recursively-constructed workspace-fiber manifolds. Experimental results on redundant nR planar manipulators demonstrate that the proposed construction preserves collision-free connectivity structure across successive lifting stages while substantially reducing collision checking complexity relative to direct configuration space reasoning.

AI.tldr: A workspace-fibered decomposition framework for motion planning in planar redundant manipulators that constructs obstacle-constrained reachable workspaces of non-redundant sub-chains and recursively lifts them through redundant orientation fibers, enabling efficient reduced-space planning with early infeasibility detection and preserved collision-free connectivity structure.
AI.motivation: Traditional motion planning for redundant manipulators operates in high-dimensional configuration spaces (n-dimensions), which becomes computationally expensive in cluttered environments due to the need for explicit configuration-space obstacle geometry construction and extensive collision checking. The authors seek a more efficient approach that preserves reachability structure while reducing computational complexity.
AI.method: The method incrementally constructs obstacle-constrained reachable workspaces of lower-dimensional non-redundant sub-chains and recursively lifts them through redundant orientation fibers using Jacobian determinant continuity constraints to enforce local inverse-kinematic branch consistency. For planar position-only manipulators, the minimal non-redundant sub-chain workspace provides exact feasibility characterization. The approach yields a sequence of reduced planning manifolds that avoid explicit full configuration-space obstacle geometry construction.
AI.result: Experimental results on redundant nR planar manipulators demonstrate that the proposed construction preserves collision-free connectivity structure across successive lifting stages while substantially reducing collision checking complexity compared to direct configuration space reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The workspace-fibered decomposition framework provides an efficient alternative to traditional configuration-space planning for redundant manipulators, enabling early infeasibility detection and maintaining branch-consistent reachability structure with significantly reduced computational cost.

title: PRISM: Privileged Probabilistic Latent Supervision for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Motion Planning
summary: End-to-end autonomous driving (E2E AD) systems integrate perception, prediction, and planning into a single differentiable architecture. While these models show great promise, their standard training often relies on output-only supervision, which can lead to weak gradients for the hidden layers of increasingly complex models. Recent works have integrated vision-language model (VLM) supervision for latent features to address this, yielding substantial empirical gains, yet leaving the underlying theoretical mechanisms poorly understood. Our investigation into this methodology reveals that the resulting performance gains stem not from VLM reasoning capabilities, as previously assumed, but rather from the latent connections forged between the E2E AD model and ground-truth (GT) data during training. Building on this insight, we propose a probabilistic deep supervision framework that regularizes intermediate latent representations directly from GT data. By treating model latents as reparameterizable distributions, we optimize the architecture via the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO). Our evaluations conducted on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that supervising trajectory-related latents with future GT paths consistently improves planning performance. Using identical training data and E2E architectures, our method achieves an 8% reduction in planning L2 error and a 3% decrease in collision rates compared to competitive vectorized baselines, all while incurring negligible computational overhead.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates vision-language model (VLM) supervision in end-to-end autonomous driving systems and discovers that its benefits stem from latent connections with ground-truth data rather than VLM reasoning. The authors propose a probabilistic deep supervision framework that regularizes intermediate latent representations using ground-truth data via the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), achieving 8% reduction in planning L2 error and 3% decrease in collision rates on nuScenes dataset.
AI.motivation: End-to-end autonomous driving (E2E AD) systems integrate perception, prediction, and planning into a single differentiable architecture, but standard output-only supervision can lead to weak gradients for hidden layers. Recent works have integrated VLM supervision for latent features, but the underlying theoretical mechanisms are poorly understood, leaving whether gains come from VLM reasoning capabilities or from latent connections with ground-truth data unclear.
AI.method: The authors investigate VLM supervision in E2E AD systems and discover that performance gains stem from latent connections with ground-truth data rather than VLM reasoning. Building on this insight, they propose a probabilistic deep supervision framework that regularizes intermediate latent representations directly from ground-truth data by treating model latents as reparameterizable distributions and optimizing via the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO).
AI.result: Evaluations on nuScenes dataset show that supervising trajectory-related latents with future ground-truth paths consistently improves planning performance. The method achieves an 8% reduction in planning L2 error and a 3% decrease in collision rates compared to competitive vectorized baselines, with negligible computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal that VLM supervision in E2E AD systems provides benefits primarily through latent connections with ground-truth data rather than VLM reasoning capabilities. The proposed probabilistic deep supervision framework offers an effective alternative that achieves substantial performance improvements while maintaining low computational cost.

title: EndoWAM: A Grounded World-Action Model for Generalizable Endoscopic Navigation
summary: Autonomous endoscopic navigation can reduce clinicians' operational burden, yet robust control remains challenging due to tissue deformation, transient occlusions, and rapidly changing viewpoints. Existing learning-based policies typically predict actions from current observations without explicitly modeling future dynamics, limiting their robustness and reliability in safety-critical settings. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling predictive visual dynamics with action generation, but extending them to robotic endoscopy remains challenging due to limited training data, restricted viewpoint diversity, deformable anatomy, and high inference latency. We present EndoWAM, which is, to our knowledge, the first WAM for generalizable robotic endoscopic navigation.
